output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency staffing. The import tool skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules and reported success. The skipped rules included the 15-second hold-off, the repeat-alarm suppression, and the routing of technical alarms to the charge phone only. Phone notifications per nurse in Pods A–C roughly doubled from 12 August, and acknowledgement time doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, was unchanged. Incident rates rose equally for core, agency and new-graduate nurses once the move happened, so staffing mix doesn't explain it. Monitor alarm volume was flat, which counts against the acuity and v7.2 software explanations. Wireless coverage looks unlikely. I'm quite confident in this. Sick leave may be linked to the alarm load, but the evidence doesn't establish that. Don't cap agency use or open performance reviews: that would punish staff for a system fault. Don't switch off phone forwarding for SpO2 and technical alarms either. Restore the 11 rules, with Clinical Engineering validation and committee sign-off. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly, and check whether sick leave eases.
